logline: A Special Forces captain and a surgeon keep colliding in Korea and in a fictional conflict zone, where their differing views on duty and love are tested by war.

renewal.note: Single-season series; concluded April 22, 2016. First Korean drama simulcast in China, exported to 32 countries. No sequel produced.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.2, first Korean drama to break 30% domestic ratings since 2012, and a pan-Asian cultural event that redefined the export potential of K-drama.

pull_quotes.text: Descendants of the Sun is addictively watchable, blending action, romance and comedy with the assurance of a show that knows exactly what it wants to be.

seasons.review_body: Descendants of the Sun was the drama that put K-drama on the international map before Netflix made the conversation mainstream. The final episode broke 30% domestic viewership - the first Korean miniseries to do so since 2012 - and the China simulcast via iQIYI turned Song Joong-ki into a Pan-Asian celebrity overnight. Kim Eun-sook's writing is in full commercial mode here: the leads are implausibly glamorous, the banter is sharp, and the war-zone setting gives the romance genuine stakes. Song Hye-kyo's surgeon Kang Mo-yeon is a stronger active agent than the genre typically allowed its heroines at the time. Critics acknowledged that the show does not pretend to be anything other than elevated popular television - and within those terms it delivers with professional efficiency. IMDb at 8.2 accurately reflects broad audience warmth rather than awards-season critical respect.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the meet-cute in a hospital, relocates to a military base, and within an hour makes the case that this show intends to be the most watchable K-drama of its year. Song Joong-ki and Song Hye-kyo's chemistry lands from the first scene.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Yoo Shi-jin returning a stolen phone - the exchange that defined the season's romantic register in ninety seconds.

critic_note.text: One of the smoothest drama premieres in recent K-drama history.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 9
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The earthquake disaster sequence that the show had been building toward - a production set piece that raised the bar for action in Korean television drama at the time. The tension between the leads reaches its first genuine breaking point as professional duty and personal feeling become incompatible.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The rescue sequence under collapsed rubble - the episode's final twenty minutes elevated the series from popular to culturally significant.

critic_note.text: Descendants of the Sun earns its action credentials here.
